greeting: Good morning, Haniel! Today the Tasks Platform gets its durable job queue — the spine of Phase 6. Then Takeoff Engine kills the ‘unnamed rooms’ demo bug and ships assemblies-per-room, closing the last pillar before estimator-grade Excel. Four high-leverage tasks in a clean window.
hype: t20 is the load-bearing piece: every sweeper job hangs on that queue. Land it first, then cross into Takeoff — label lane v2 (t26) fixes the Harborview demo bug, and assemblies-per-room (t18) is the last pillar between you and the real Excel. Afternoon closes the loop: t29’s cross-process refresh lock and t22’s CI lane are the two gates before you can flip SWEEPER_REPOS to live. Solid ratio (0.88) — tight but doable. Let’s go.

schedule.title: Durable job queue (lease/heartbeat/reclaim, window-aware, priority, cap)
schedule.prep: Open the task queue module. Implement lease/heartbeat/reclaim: a job row with lease_expires_at; the daemon heartbeats every N seconds; a reclaimer re-queues expired leases. Must be window-aware (won’t start a job after the work window closes) and enforce a concurrency cap. Exit criteria: a job survives a daemon restart mid-lease and gets reclaimed; two concurrent jobs can’t exceed the cap.

schedule.title: Label lane v2: M3 vision for outlined-text firms + callout-vs-room filtering
schedule.prep: Open engine/labels.py (and the run_labels_m3tiles.py spike). Bug: rooms show ‘unnamed’ because PDFTron outlines all text — the free live-text lane finds nothing. v2 = (a) productize the M3 tiles lane as an opt-in ‘read labels (AI)’ action (MINIMAX_AI key must reach the VPS — that’s a secrets decision); (b) callout-vs-room filtering to exclude general-note paragraphs, UP arrows, FEC callouts. Exit criteria: Harborview demo PDF shows named rooms in the lane panel.

schedule.title: Assemblies-per-room → paint/drywall/flooring quantities + wall heights
schedule.prep: Open engine/assemblies.py. Implement room type → assembly formulas: paint (net wall area minus openings), drywall (gross wall + ceiling), flooring (floor area). Heights come from wall_height_ft. Output drives the 5-tab Excel export. Exit criteria: a real CT Pros PDF produces per-room assembly quantities in the Excel workbook — this closes the last pillar before the estimator-grade deliverable.

schedule.title: Daemon-side cross-process refresh lock (prereq for live SWEEPER_REPOS)
schedule.prep: Open the daemon’s job lifecycle code. The refresh CLI already uses a per-repo O_EXCL single-flight lockfile (CLI-vs-CLI). The daemon must honor the SAME per-repo lock across a job’s whole lifecycle — its current per-job lock is in-process and cannot see the CLI’s file. Implement: daemon acquires the per-repo lock before any repo-touching work, holds through completion. Exit criteria: refresh CLI while daemon holds the lock blocks or fails cleanly; no silent conflict. Until this ships, run refresh ONLY while the sweeper is stopped.

schedule.title: Unprivileged CI lane + sensitive-path human gate
schedule.prep: Design the CI pipeline so the sweeper’s test runner has NO access to secrets and never runs under pull_request_target. Separate the privileged deploy job (needs secrets, runs only on main after CI passes) from the unprivileged test job (runs on all branches). Add the sensitive-path gate: if a job touches auth/deploy/config paths, escalate to the decision inbox before shipping. Exit criteria: a test run with no secrets env reveals no leaked credentials; a PR touching a gated path routes to the human inbox.
